skill.name: codebase-mapping

security_audit.summary: The helper script performs local repository analysis and has no network behavior in the reviewed files. One Markdown command invokes the bundled Python script, and the script can write to a user-supplied output path. The remaining SKILL.md alerts are Markdown formatting or inline examples, and the environment-file alert is dotfile exclusion logic.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running the Python helper script and show the target repository path.

remediation.issue: User-supplied output path can overwrite files
remediation.suggestion: Refuse to overwrite existing files unless a force option is supplied, or default output to a safe report directory.

content.value_statement: Large repositories are difficult to understand before review or modification. This skill maps structure, dependencies, entry points, and key files.
actual_capabilities: Generates a filtered file tree for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and package metadata files.
Extracts Python imports with AST parsing.
Extracts JavaScript and TypeScript import and require statements with pattern matching.
Identifies common Python and Node entry points.
Flags key files for types, execution, tools, agents, and configuration.
Writes a structured JSON map or prints the map to the console.
limitations: It does not execute project code or resolve runtime dependencies.
JavaScript parsing is pattern-based and may miss dynamic imports.
Hidden files are excluded except .env.example, so hidden configuration is not mapped.
It reads local repositories only and has no network integration.

use_cases.title: Onboard to an unfamiliar repository
use_cases.description: Create a concise map of directories, entry points, dependencies, and key files before making changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare an architecture review
use_cases.description: Identify module boundaries and dependency groups before deeper technical analysis.

use_cases.title: Scope AI-assisted code analysis
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code a focused map before asking for targeted investigation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first map
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the codebase-mapping skill on this repository. Generate a structure map and summarize the main directories, entry points, and dependency groups.

prompt_templates.title: Find key entry points
prompt_templates.prompt: Map this repository and identify the files most likely to start the application, command line tools, tests, or package exports.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a module review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the repository map to group internal modules, list important dependencies, and recommend which files need manual architecture review.

prompt_templates.title: Scope deeper investigations
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the mapper, inspect dependencies and key files, then propose the minimal file set for analyzing data models, execution flow, and agent control loops.

output_examples.input: Map a Python service before onboarding.
output: A structure summary with primary packages, support folders, and generated file counts.
Likely entry points such as application modules, package setup files, and executable modules.
Key files grouped by types, execution, tools, agents, and configuration.

output_examples.input: Prepare an architecture review for a TypeScript package.
output: A dependency overview that separates external packages from internal module references.
A short list of files that should be reviewed first for public interfaces and runtime flow.
Notes about parsing limits where dynamic imports may require manual checking.

output_examples.input: Create context for an AI code investigation.
output: A concise repository map that can guide Claude, Codex, or Claude Code toward relevant files.
Suggested analysis targets for follow-up work, grouped by architecture concern.

best_practices: Run the mapper on repositories you are authorized to inspect.
Choose an output path inside a safe report directory.
Review generated entry points manually before making architectural decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the map as a complete security review.
Do not run the helper against private repositories without permission.
Do not overwrite important files with the output path.

faq.question: Does this skill send code to a network service?
faq.answer: No network behavior was found in the reviewed skill files. The helper script analyzes local repository files.

faq.question: Which languages does it inspect?
faq.answer: It inspects Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, and TSX files for dependency mapping.

faq.question: Can it parse every import style?
faq.answer: No. Python parsing uses AST, while JavaScript and TypeScript parsing uses patterns that may miss dynamic imports.

faq.question: Does it include secrets in the map?
faq.answer: The file tree excludes hidden files except .env.example. Dependency extraction reads source files but does not target secret stores.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a repository map with file tree, dependency overview, entry points, key files, and basic statistics.
